#Part A — Creating Vectors and List
```{r}
worker_age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

length(worker_age)

min(worker_age)
max(worker_age)

worker_age[c(13:18, 33:35)]
worker_age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]

worker_age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
worker_age

data(rivers)

river <- c(length(rivers), sum(rivers), mean(rivers), median(rivers), var(rivers), sd(rivers), min(rivers), max(rivers))
river

power_ranking <- c(1:25)
power_ranking

celebrity_name <- c ("Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2", "Tiger Woods", "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent", "Cast of the Sopranos", "Dan Brown", "Bruce Springsteen", "Donald Trump", "Muhammad Ali", "Paul McCartney", "George Lucas", "Elton John", "David Letterman", "Phil Mickelson", "J.K. Rowling", "Bradd Pitt", "Peter Jackson", "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Jay Leno", "Celine Dion", "Kobe Bryant")

pay <- c(67, 90, 225, 110, 90, 332, 302, 41, 52, 88, 55, 44, 55, 40, 233, 34, 40, 47, 75, 25, 39, 45, 32, 40, 31)

power_ranking[celebrity_name == "J.K. Rowling"] <- 15
power_ranking
pay[celebrity_name == "J.K. Rowling"] <- 90
pay

vegetables_list <- list("Broccoli", "Carrot", "Spinach", "Squash", "Potato", "Eggplant", "Cabbage", "Asparagus", "Bell Pepper", "Bok Choy")
vegetables_list <- append(vegetables_list, list("Cucumber", "Onion"))
vegetables_list

length(vegetables_list)

vegetables_list <- append(vegetables_list, list("Beetroot", "Celery", "Water Spinanch", "Turnip"), after = 5)
vegetables_list

length(vegetables_list)

```
#Question 1
#A factory has a census of its workers. There are 50 workers in total. The following list shows their ages: `34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.


a. Create a vector for the worker’s age.
  worker_age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
  
b. How many data points?
  There are 50 data points.
  
c. Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker’s age.
  The minimum value of worker's age is 17. min(worker_age)
  The maximum value of worker's age is 61. max(worker_age)
  
d. Access the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s Age.
  To acces the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35 elements of worker's age, just enter
    worker_age[c(13:18, 33:35)]
    
    output: 27 22 37 34 19 20 33 41 53
    
e. Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included.
       code: worker_age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]
      
    output: [1] 34 28 22 36 27 18 52 39 42 35 31 27 22 37 34 19 20 57 50 37 46 25 17 37 43 53 41 35 24 33 41 53 40
            [34] 18 44 38 48 27 39 19 30 61 54 58 26 18

f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.
    worker_age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
    worker_age
    
    output: [1] 34 28 22  0 27 18 52 39 42 29 35 31 27  0 37 34 19 20 57 49 50 37 46  0 17 37 43 53 41 51 35 24 33
            [34] 41 53 40 18 44 38 41 48 27 39  0 30 61 54 58 26 18
            

#Question 2

a. Get the number of elements (length) in rivers, their sum (sum), mean (mean), median(median), variance(var), standard deviation(sd), minimum (min) and maximum (max).
  
  river <- c(length(rivers), sum(rivers), mean(rivers), median(rivers), var(rivers), sd(rivers), min(rivers), max(rivers))
river

  To get:   
    length = 141.0000
    sum = 83357.0000
    mean = 591.1844
    median = 425.0000
    var = 243908.4086
    sd = 493.8708
    min = 135.0000
    max = 3710.0000

#Question 4

Create a list of ten (10) vegetables you ate during your lifetime. If none, just list down the vegetables in your mind.

  vegetables_list <- list("Broccoli", "Carrot", "Spinach", "Squash", "Potato", "Eggplant", "Cabbage", "Asparagus", "Bell Pepper", "Bok Choy")
  
a. Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list. What is the result?

  vegetables_list <- append(vegetables_list, list("Cucumber", "Onion"))
vegetables_list

b. How many datapoints do you have?
  There are 12 data points.
  
c. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?
 
  vegetables_list <- append(vegetables_list, list("Beetroot", "Celery", "Water Spinanch", "Turnip"), after = 5)
  vegetables_list


d. How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?
  Now we have 16 data points.
